verdicts.claim: CI's data job gates the deploy, so a data-shape change without its schema cannot ship.
verdicts.what_is_true: The wiring is real: deploy needs data (ci.yml:528), so the gate fails closed. But ci.yml has run 0 jobs on every push since 3c9005ac (latest run 42419094149: 0 jobs), and the data job checks HEAD's data, not the pinned 257a766c tree that /play/ serves (tools/site-pin.mjs never calls the validator). So 'cannot ship' holds only because nothing ships at all. handoff.md:52 does not mention the gate.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It reads as a live check, so nobody noticed 37 unvalidated pushes. The lint that catches the YAML break sits inside the same dead data job.
verdicts.fix: Correct CLAUDE.md:112: the data job checks HEAD only and is dead until the four step names are quoted. Run node tools/check-workflows.mjs before every push, and validate the pinned tree in the site job.

verdicts.claim: Real names and identifying paths stay out of public files and the owner stays pseudonymous; Windows user-name paths were to be replaced (M5, S1); Orb should check the GitHub handle; the copyright-line name is open.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is breached in the public repo. 52 tracked files at HEAD (67 lines) hold the local Windows user-profile path, up from Legal's 3. vision.md:71 has given a personal name (first name and surname initial) as 'Copyright holder' since 701c76a0 (2026-09-29), and vision.md:1403 names Orb's US state. Git history keeps all of it. Commit emails are GitHub no-reply addresses. I could not check whether the handle is a legal name.
verdicts.fix: Ask Orb one question: keep the name and state public or not. If not, remove them from vision.md and replace the user-profile path in the 52 files. History keeps the old copies unless Orb chooses a rewrite.

verdicts.claim: Desktop-build CI artifacts in the public repo are not covered by the flash interim; they may run only after Orb's one-sentence yes, with 1-day retention, pin-move readings passed, RL-196's fix landed, the lock on and no link.
key_sources: homework/2 Up Next/09 Business - Legal's open questions (10 min).md:8
verdicts.what_is_true: desktop-builds.yml applies most of RL-203: retention-days 1, the lock and route checks. Its 'Orb's yes' is only a date-format check, and it never checks the pin-move readings (condition 2). It has never run. linux-export.yml bypasses the gate entirely: it uploads a Linux game binary for 14 days with no yes step and no lock, and the tree ships lock_reduce_flashing false. It has never run either, and the repo holds no game artifacts today.
external: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/download-workflow-artifacts (accessed 2026-11-07): "Read access to the repository is required to perform these steps."
verdicts.fix: Give linux-export.yml the RL-203 refusal, the lock and route steps and 1-day retention, or retire it. Make desktop-builds.yml check the pin-move record for the commit.

verdicts.claim: Before each re-pin of the public demo Orb gets the link and a 30-second clip; a look-changing re-pin waits for Orb's word or a day's notice; a visible change needs a side-by-side; on 2026-10-05 an EP docs push put an unready slice live for an hour.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is real (ADR 0010 item 6, playbook 8), but it is Orb's look and creative direction, and the 2026-10-05 slip was about balance, not safety. Since 2026-10-18 the pinned deploy (ci.yml:476-486) stops a main push from changing /play/. The pin has been 257a766c since 45869fac (2026-10-19, on Orb's word), so the 2026-11-05 deploy was not a re-pin.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A taste rule pads the safety ledger. The inventory's note that the 2026-11-05 deploy lacked Orb's clip treats a rebuild of the same pin as a re-pin.
verdicts.fix: Move it to EP process under ADR 0010. Correct the note: the 2026-11-05 deploy did not move the pin.

verdicts.claim: The native ENet link is 'built and tested between two programs in CI', and enet_check runs only in CI, never on Orb's PC, because a socket could raise a firewall prompt.
verdicts.what_is_true: The two-process ENet steps (added cf90189c) passed in the last green CI run, 41956488028 at 72a4d1e4. net/enet_transport.gd gained redial() in 3c9005ac, after that run, so the LAN build a8bc66e2 ships ENet code CI never ran. The --late-host step has never run and appears twice (ci.yml:417, 419). The firewall-prompt rule is machine discipline; I could not check whether it was followed.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A test-coverage statement and a dev-PC rule sit in the safety records, and the record overstates coverage of the build Orb and Orb 2 have.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Netcode's test record. Correct it to 'two-process tested at 72a4d1e4; redial and late host untested'. Drop the duplicate step.

verdicts.claim: The GDScript goldens are checked by tools/parity.gd on every push (CI, Linux) and locally.
verdicts.what_is_true: The step exists (ci.yml:188-189) and last passed in run 41956488028 at 72a4d1e4 (2026-11-05). Since then sim/core/test/golden.json changed in 3c9005ac and a8bc66e2 with no CI check, because CI runs no jobs. Local runs leave no record. It is a determinism gate, not a release-safety one.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It adds a determinism gate to the safety ledger, and 'every push' hides that two golden regenerations went unchecked.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Simulation/QA. Once ci.yml parses again, re-run parity on HEAD and say the gate was down from 3c9005ac.

verdicts.claim: World's step_check exits 0 even when it fails, which hides failures behind a passing gate.
verdicts.what_is_true: It does exit 0 every time (step_check.gd:149-150 ends on a plain quit()). Since 0ca00c3e (2026-10-30), CI runs it through tools/gate.mjs --verdict, which reads 'STEP: 1 check(s) failed' as a failure (reproduced with verdictProblems). So it hides nothing in CI. Its failures were wall-clock budget flakes under load.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It suggests a hole in the gates that the verdict wrapper already closes, inviting rework, and it is a QA tooling note carried as a safety bug.
verdicts.fix: Retire it from the safety records. Record step_check's timing flake under World/QA, and note that it is safe only through gate.mjs --verdict.

verdicts.claim: Nothing enters the repo or a build without a register row and an accepted licence, exact versions pinned; GPL/AGPL, NC/ND, unlicensed, fan-game and commercially barred AI output are rejected; no OrbCombat or other GPL code copied in.
verdicts.what_is_true: Mostly in force. Versions are pinned and the lockfile is committed (Part D item 2 is stale). No GPL text or SPDX headers appear outside docs except Godot's own licence texts, and there are no addons or GDExtensions. upload-artifact, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages have no register row, but all three are MIT and CI-only. LR-005 still says there is no audio while 108 audio files are tracked; I did not check their origin. I ran no snippet-level scan.
verdicts.fix: Legal adds rows for the three Pages and artifact actions, closes Part D item 2 and updates LR-005 for the tracked audio.

verdicts.claim: Never commit the Steamworks SDK, its headers or binaries, or any console SDK to the public repo; Steam code stays desktop-only; GodotSteam terms read first; Legal reads the Steam Distribution Agreement before Orb signs.
verdicts.what_is_true: The basis is stated correctly: s1.1 of the agreement allows redistribution of only redistributable_bin. No Steam SDK-like path exists in HEAD or anywhere in history, and no GDScript calls a Steam singleton. Nothing in .gitignore or CI would stop a future commit; the rule is honour-system.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/documentation/sdk_access_agreement (accessed 2026-11-07), s1.1(b): "reproduce and distribute the part of the SDK provided inside the folder named redistributable_bin"
verdicts.fix: Before Steam work starts, add a CI path check that rejects steam_api, redistributable_bin and sdk/public paths.

verdicts.claim: The desktop package README gives no assurances ('safe', 'tested', 'verified', 'virus-free', 'compliant') and warns that the file is not signed with a publisher certificate.
verdicts.what_is_true: Enforced in code: tools/desktop-package.mjs checks for NO_ASSURANCE words and requires WINDOWS_WARN. The READMEs I generated with the active notice have no banned word, and the Windows and macOS ones say the file is unsigned. Linux has no signing line, and RL-204 asks for none. No desktop package has ever been built (0 desktop-builds runs), and the binaries would be unsigned (desktop-builds.yml:9).
verdicts.fix: None needed now. Keep the verify step in any future packaging path, including linux-export.yml.

verdicts.claim: AI-written code is reviewed before merge; long verbatim snippets and foreign licence headers are rejected; a licence scanner is used when in doubt.
verdicts.what_is_true: Nothing shows the review happens. There have been 0 PRs and 0 merges: 2744 commits went straight to an unprotected main, 2695 with a Claude co-author line. No licence scanner exists, and no record shows a check for verbatim snippets. A header grep of the code folders finds no foreign licence headers. The cited case is real: the Ninth Circuit affirmed in Doe v. GitHub, No. 24-7700, filed 2026-09-16.
external: https://cdn.ca9.uscourts.gov/datastore/opinions/2026/09/16/24-7700.pdf (accessed 2026-11-07): "plaintiffs did not state a claim under the DMCA"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: The record gives false comfort that the code's provenance is checked when no test exists.
verdicts.fix: Write the missing test: a CI grep for foreign licence, SPDX and copyright headers in shipped folders, plus one snippet-scanner pass before any store build.

verdicts.claim: The webrtc-native GDExtension would be a new dependency and needs approval before native-to-browser cross-play.
verdicts.what_is_true: This is accurate: Godot's docs say native WebRTC needs an external GDExtension. No WebRTC file, GDExtension or register row exists, and no GDScript uses WebRTC classes. Online play is after launch (vision.md:32). It is a dependency and scope decision, already covered by register rule 1, not a safety matter.
external: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/networking/webrtc.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "require an external GDExtension plugin on native (non-HTML5) platforms"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A future-feature dependency question adds a line to the safety ledger and nothing else.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Netcode's open items, and route it through a licence-register row when cross-play is scoped.

verdicts.claim: CI pins actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to commit SHAs, and Legal registers them as CI-only.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every external action in all six workflows is pinned to a full SHA, and each SHA matches its commented tag (checked with the GitHub API). The local setup-godot action checks every download with SHA-512, and every workflow has contents: read. checkout and setup-node are registered as CI-only (LR-020/021). The other three actions have no row (see AC-245).
verdicts.fix: None for pinning. Add the three missing register rows (AC-245).

batch_notes: The most serious finding in this slice is outside the claims: CI has been dead since 3c9005ac (0 jobs per run; tools/check-workflows.mjs fails at HEAD on ci.yml:226, 240, 263 and 277). The lint that would have caught this runs only inside the dead data job.
Gap behind AC-240: linux-export.yml can upload a desktop game binary with the Reduce flashing lock off, for 14 days, with no RL-203 refusal. It has never run.

Inventory corrections: AC-241's 2026-11-05 deploy did not move the pin (257a766c since 2026-10-19). AC-244 is already handled by gate.mjs --verdict. AC-238's data job validates HEAD, not the pinned tree.
AC-239 exposes personal data. The verify JSON and AC-239.txt keep the name and state redacted, but the public repo and its history still carry them.
I could not check: whether the GitHub handle is a legal name, local parity runs, or whether ENet was ever run on Orb's PC.
